sentences.text: Hybodus possessed two dorsal fins, one of which featured a bony plate likely used for defense.
This shark had two distinct types of teeth: sharper ones for catching slippery prey and flatter ones to crush shelled animals.
Males possessed pterigopodia, specialized organs that directly inserted sperm into the female during mating.
A preserved specimen of Hybodus hauffianus was found with over 100 belemnite rostra in its stomach.
Hybodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the family Hybodontidae, and the parent group Hybodontinae.

Several species previously assigned to Hybodus from the Cretaceous have been transferred to the genus Meristodonoides, while some Triassic species are not hybodonts and belong to the order Synechodontiformes.
Specifically, the species H. reticulatus and H. hauffianus are known from the Early Jurassic of Europe.
